No spec subject (candidates: specled.append_only when picked up). Severity: Medium. From 2026-08-06 critical review of specled_-q0q. authorizing_decision/2 matches an ADR by change_type/affects without checking its status field, so a superseded or rejected ADR in the same PR still suppresses weakening findings. Keep-reason: interacts with the F1 uniform-emission design decision (same choke point); landing it separately risks two conflicting authorization contracts. Concrete failure: a PR carrying a rejected ADR whose affects lists x.req_a gets its weakening of x.req_a silently authorized.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.append_only

BLOCKED BY specled_-bg5.1. Both tickets must change authorizing_decision/2
(lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:698-722): bg5.1 changes what it RETURNS and how its result is
consumed; this ticket changes what it ACCEPTS. bg5.1 settles the authorization contract first;
this ticket then adds one predicate inside that settled shape. Reversed, this ticket writes a
status gate into a shape bg5.1 immediately deletes.

DECISION-CLASS: yes — spec amendment required, ADR recommended. The ticket does NOT
self-describe this. specled.append_only.requirement_deleted (.spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:47-57)
defines authorization purely as "no head-side ADR in the weakening set lists the removed id in
its affects". Status is not a term in the requirement, so adding a gate makes the statement
FALSE and it must be amended. The amendment NARROWS what authorizes (a strengthening), so no
authorizing ADR is required for the spec edit itself — but record the status/authorization
interaction alongside specled.decision.change_type_enum_v1 and specled.decision.adr_append_only.
Per operator ruling on epic specled_-i4x: draft fully, record completion normally; the
orchestrator will NOT merge without human sign-off.

CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN BODY: "rejected" is NOT a legal ADR status. The schema enum is
~w(accepted deprecated superseded) — lib/specled_ex/schema/decision.ex:5 and :13 — so a
"rejected" ADR fails schema parse and never reaches the detector. Live exposure is DEPRECATED
and SUPERSEDED, both legal, both currently authorizing weakenings indefinitely. Implement
against those two.

SECOND SURFACE THE TICKET MISSES: self_authorizing_adrs/2 (lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:640-661)
also ignores status, so a new-in-diff deprecated ADR still drives both the
same_pr_self_authorization warning and the deletion-path marker at :132-138. Fixing only
authorizing_decision/2 leaves the two functions disagreeing. status is read exactly once in the
whole module today — :314, inside adr_affects_widened, gating on == "accepted".

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex
- .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md
- test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs
- test_support/append_only_fixtures.ex
- .spec/realization_hashes.json
- CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/schema/decision.ex  (do NOT extend the status enum)
- lib/specled_ex/decision_parser*
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT add a `rejected` status. That is a schema + governance ticket of its own.
- Do NOT restructure marker emission — that is bg5.1. Add the status gate inside the shape
  bg5.1 leaves behind.
- Do NOT mint a new finding code for status-blocked weakenings without a budget amendment.
  Reuse append_only/requirement_deleted etc., which falls out naturally when
  authorizing_decision/2 returns :none.
- Do NOT change adr_affects_widened's == "accepted" gate at :314.

Verification:
  mix test test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs
  mix test test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format --check-formatted
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
No stub to flip; new scenarios attach to the existing execute:true block
(.spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:400-417).

Expected diff: ~70-120 lines across 4-5 files.

At `accepted` the emitted codes are exactly ["append_only/same_pr_self_authorization", "append_only/self_authorized_weakening"] — BOTH refuted codes actually fire. At "deprecated"/"superseded" the codes are exactly ["append_only/requirement_deleted"]. Every one of the three assertions in the new test flips when status flips, so none is trivially satisfied. The test is also well constructed in that it pairs the two refutes with a positive `assert requirement_deleted` — that rules out the "scenario produced no findings at all" failure mode inline.

Caveat worth recording (not a defect): the predicate is an equality allowlist (`status == "accepted"`), so every non-accepted value takes the identical branch — I confirmed a fabricated "bogus_unknown_status" yields byte-identical output to both. The "superseded" iteration therefore adds no discriminating power over "deprecated"; it is redundant rather than an overclaim, and the allowlist shape is fail-closed on unknown/malformed statuses, which is the right default.

Residual gap, recommendation not blocker: if a future refactor inlines the gate per-call-site and drops it from one of the three uncovered detectors, this test stays green.

Both gated surfaces were mutated independently and each mutant turns the suite red on a distinct assertion line, so neither gate is silently untested. The only shortfalls are cosmetic-to-minor (the superseded iteration is redundant under an equality allowlist; coverage is the deletion detector only, mitigated by the gate living in the shared helper), and neither rises to a hole in what the test establishes.

No AUDIT: APPROVE marker posted: that token instructs a fast-forward merge, and this ticket carries
a spec amendment plus a new ADR needing a human decision. It is also STACKED on specled_-bg5.1,
which is itself held — merging this without that would be incoherent. The trail ends at
VERIFY: PASS + TEST_CRITIC: PASS, which the resume table maps back to the Selective Audit Gate.

WHAT THE OPERATOR IS SIGNING OFF ON: specled.decision.accepted_adr_authorization plus an amendment
to specled.append_only.requirement_deleted. The requirement defined authorization purely as "no
head-side ADR in the weakening set lists the removed id in its affects" — status was not a term in
it, so adding a status gate makes the statement false and it must be amended. The amendment NARROWS
what authorizes, which is a strengthening.

THE TICKET AS FILED DESCRIBED AN IMPOSSIBLE CASE. It claimed a "rejected" ADR still authorizes
weakenings. There is no rejected status: the schema enum is ~w(accepted deprecated superseded)
(lib/specled_ex/schema/decision.ex:5, :13), so such an ADR fails schema parse and never reaches the
detector. The real exposure is DEPRECATED and SUPERSEDED — both legal, both previously authorizing

A SECOND UNGATED SURFACE, not in the ticket body, was found during contract synthesis and is fixed
here: self_authorizing_adrs/2 also ignored status, and it drives the same-PR self-authorization
warning independently of authorizing_decision/3. Gating only one would have left the two functions
disagreeing — a deprecated new-in-diff ADR would stop authorizing but keep emitting the warning.

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE. The verifier drove analyze/3 directly at each status and built a truth table
rather than reading the code:
  ADR new-in-diff:  accepted -> [same_pr_self_authorization, self_authorized_weakening]  (deletion suppressed)

                    superseded -> [requirement_deleted]

                    deprecated -> [requirement_deleted]
                    superseded -> [requirement_deleted]
The second block isolates the authorizing_decision gate independently of new-in-diff status, and
the `accepted` row is the non-vacuity control.

THE TEST IS BUILT ON REFUTES, which is the shape most likely to be vacuous — a refute passes
trivially if the scenario never produced the finding. The critic proved otherwise by execution:
with the byte-identical fixture and only `status` varied, at `accepted` BOTH refuted codes actually
fire. Every assertion flips when status flips. The test also pairs the refutes with a positive
assert, ruling out "no findings at all" inline.

PER-SURFACE MUTANTS BOTH RED, independently — neither surface free-rides on the other:
  authorizing_decision/3 gate removed only  -> RED at the positive assert (deletion re-authorized)
  self_authorizing_adrs/2 gate removed only -> RED at the same-PR refute (warning re-emitted)

Caveat recorded, not a defect: the predicate is an equality allowlist (status == "accepted"), so
every non-accepted value takes the identical branch — a fabricated unknown status behaves exactly
like deprecated. That is the conservative direction and consistent with the schema being closed.

bg5.1's order-independence and lexicographic tie-break properties were re-run and still hold; this
ticket added one predicate inside that settled selection shape rather than restructuring it.

APPROVED. Merged into specled_-i4x/fast-follow-backlog. Closing per operator sign-off.

Merged as a6a62b66. Full merge gate GREEN: compile clean, format clean, deps.unlock clean,
MIX_ENV=test make xref at zero compile-connected edges, mix test 1342 tests / 3 properties /
0 failures, bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh -> validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0;
spec.check result=pass.

THE STACK UNWOUND CORRECTLY, which was the one real risk in merging this chain. This branch was cut
from specled_-bg5.1's tip and CONTAINED bg5.1's two commits. bg5.1 was rebased onto the epic before
merging, so its work landed under different SHAs. The rebase worker was instructed to verify — not
assume — that exactly ONE commit survived, and to abort and report if two or three did, since that
would mean re-applying bg5.1's changes onto a branch that already has them. Result: 1 commit, the
four expected files, realization_hashes.json diff empty. Git recognised the duplicated patches and
skipped them.

What landed: specled.decision.accepted_adr_authorization (change_type: clarifies — authorizes no
weakening) plus an amendment to specled.append_only.requirement_deleted adding a status gate.
Deprecated and superseded ADRs no longer authorize weakenings or emit self-authorization findings.

Worth restating what this fixed, because the ticket as filed described an impossible case: it
claimed a "rejected" ADR still authorizes. There is no rejected status — the schema enum is
accepted | deprecated | superseded, so such an ADR fails parse and never reaches the detector. The
real exposure was DEPRECATED and SUPERSEDED, both legal and both authorizing indefinitely. A second
ungated surface (self_authorizing_adrs/2) was also found during contract synthesis and is fixed
here; gating only authorizing_decision would have left the two functions disagreeing.

Unblocks specled_-bg5.6, which is stacked on this branch.
